acceptance: Every one of the 89 FAIL bundles is listed with its failing checks and a verdict (data defect, validator defect, or unknown with the reason), reproduced by running the command, not copied from this item.
For sf1_row_counts and required_keys, the record shows on at least two bundles what the validator expected and what the bundle holds, and states which side is wrong.

Data defects are mapped to existing items (rerun-cloud-bundles-defective-dbgen, duckdb-sf10-tpch-defective-datagen-rerun, corpus-tpch-shallow-cohort-replacements-20261018) or to a new item; ranked defective results are raised with the owner for withdrawal or exclusion.
Validator defects are filed as one item with failing test cases; the validator is not changed under this item.
context: Source: found on 2026-11-13 while delivering the agent-facing work (PRs BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4202, #4203 and BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site#152, #153, #154). Read-only triage; no corpus, ranking or validator change here. Do this before the corpus reruns, because it may change what needs rerunning. Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items share one feature branch and PR where their files overlap. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy and add a changelog.d fragment for user-facing changes. Re-verify every cited file and line before acting; they are hints. Stop and report rather than widen scope.
description:
Problem: running the new `benchbox results validate` over results-data/bundles gave 491 bundles: 379 PASS, 23 WARN, 89 FAIL. 74 of the 89 FAIL bundles are ranking-eligible by the Explorer pipeline's own functions. 47 fail only sf1_row_counts, 15 only required_keys, 12 both; by platform BigQuery 25, Snowflake 25, ClickHouse Local 6, DataFusion 6, DuckDB 6, Databricks 4, SQLite 2. Either ranked public results are defective, or the validator raises false failures. Both matter: the first misleads readers, the second makes the new command untrustworthy.

Outcome: each failing check classified as a real data defect or a validator defect, with evidence, and the follow-up routed: reruns or withdrawals through the existing corpus items and takedown process, validator fixes as a separate change.
